newsitem.title: UK: UK wise man' Bootle says UK inflation set to fall.
newsitem.headline: UK wise man' Bootle says UK inflation set to fall.

text.p: HSBC Group chief economist Roger Bootle, a member of the British Treasury's panel of independent forecasters or "wise men", said on Thursday British inflation was set to fall this year and that worries about it were overblown.
Bootle forecasts underlying inflation at 2.25 percent by year-end. He said people were underestimating the effects of a strong pound and also of competition among British retailers.

"Not for the first time people in the markets and the media are getting scared about inflation quite out of proportion to the situation on the ground," Bootle told Reuters following release of March retail price data.

Underlying inflation, which excludes mortgage interest payments, rose by 0.3 percent in March, bringing the annual rate down to 2.7 percent from 2.9 percent in February, the Office for National Statistics said on Thursday.
"Far from rising this year, inflation is going to fall, said Bootle, author of a book entitled The Death of Inflation'.

He noted that the underlying inflation rate was only narrowly above the government's 2.5 percent target while the RPIY measure, which excludes mortgage payments and indirect taxes, was below it at 2.3 percent.
"All this is despite the effects of big increases in petrol prices, reflecting the rise in international oil prices last year which is now being reversed," Bootle said.
